Intro: Well, don't look at me like that. Of course, I've kept watch over you.
My subordinates are fond of visiting, if only to waste breath on your silence.
How droll is the common man, to spend his days prostrating in servitude or fruitlessly shouting in the streets.
If you want real change, then don't close your eyes when you fire the gun. Watch as the blood sputters from a mouth agape.
The rebellion can't decide who lives and who dies, so they fire indiscriminately into the crowd, calling it revolution.
I saved Verehn once. I have had enough of watching bull-headed fools drive themselves mad with delusion, dragging us all down with them.
Go on. I'd like to see what you can do, chef.
This won't save you, of course.
But you may share this last meal with me on death row.
Success: Hm. Startlingly mediocre.
I watched the old royalty glut themselves, salivating over the untrimmed fat, rolling oil glistening down their chins.
But just beyond the doors of their gilded palaces, I watched street children grow into their skin with no muscles; just tendon, sinew, and bone.
The wealth within their walls could've pulled every single one of those children out of poverty, fed every hungry mouth.
But as small, emaciated bodies outside crawled into each other's arms for heat, the nauseating sound of chewing and slurping persisted.
How could they still want? After they ate their fill, they hoarded the leftovers and forced themselves to swallow just so someone else could not eat.
This city was too weak-willed to free itself. Someone had to step in and save them.
And now you stand in my way again, fraternizing with rebels who don't know what it means to be free.
It was a good attempt. I admire your blind faith in foolish resolve.
This is the end of the line for you.

Success: Surely you don't believe I'd fall for such a shallow ploy. I have seen you allow the rebels to flit around your establishment as they please.
And yet it is tempting. It reminds me of someone.
It was a good attempt. I admire your blind faith in foolish resolve.
Perhaps I'll let you die from this dish.
A fitting end, don't you think?

Success: Not bad for what you've got.
I respect your resourcefulness. You make do with what you have, and it's almost quality.
Restaurants like yours are expendable. We will no longer need your service.
This establishment will be closed, and you will be—
What's this?
…Baklava? You should not have given me this.
Baklava… it is indulgent. In a way, an antithesis of everything I've built. Sticky, sweet, messy—encased in a fragile shell built to be broken.
I spent decades in pharmacology. I executed every procedure and experiment with pinpoint accuracy.
My work is, and always has been, of logic and precision. That is how I rule Verehn.
I do not cave to pleasure, that sweet, oily sheen that coats your tongue.
The Moshchny—they fed themselves and their people on frivolous indulgence and sugar, making them fat and lazy with content.
This was made to be flaky, dripping. It's supposed to coat your fingers in a sticky sweet film, to be licked off with a smile.
Like an opium for the masses. Obsessive, addictive, and easy. Reminds those who eat of it of a softer, kinder time.
Sustenance is the cornerstone of our civilization, and indulgence of it, our culture. This baklava…
I forget myself.
